# Introduction and Problem Statement

<!-- Member 1: Replace this comment with the final project background, motivation, research question and stakeholder relevance. -->

This project investigates how accurately information available before kick-off can classify football matches as a **home win**, **draw** or **away win** across Europe's top five domestic leagues.

**Research question:** How accurately can football match outcomes be classified using only information available before kick-off?

# Data and Feature Engineering

<!-- Member 2: Summarise the data source, filtering, target construction and leakage controls. -->

The modelling dataset contains matches from the top domestic leagues of England, Spain, Italy, Germany and France. All predictors are calculated using information available strictly before each fixture.

## Engineered predictors

<!-- Member 2: Explain the final differential features and why they were selected. -->

- League-table position difference
- Season points-per-game difference
- Recent-form points difference
- Recent goal-difference form
- Home-versus-away venue-form difference
- Head-to-head difference
- Rest-days difference
- Competition and season progress

## Outcome distribution

```{r}
#| label: outcome-distribution
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of match outcomes in the modelling dataset."
outcome_plot <- as.data.table(model_data)[, .N, by = result]
outcome_plot[, share := N / sum(N)]

ggplot(outcome_plot, aes(result, share, fill = result)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = false) +
  geom_text(aes(label = pct(share)), vjust = -0.3) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of matches") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Preprocessing and Validation Strategy

<!-- Member 3: Consolidate the shared preprocessing and evaluation design. -->

The analysis uses a chronological split. Seasons through 2022/23 form the training period, while seasons from 2023/24 onward form the untouched Final Test. Five expanding-window validation folds inside the training period support feature selection and hyperparameter tuning.

The primary model-selection metric is **Macro-F1**, supported by Accuracy, Balanced Accuracy, class-level Precision, Recall and F1, and confusion matrices.

# Model Evaluation and Final Model Selection

```{r}
#| label: model-comparison
comparison_files <- list.files(
  "outputs",
  pattern = "^member[1-5]_.*comparison_row\\.csv$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

comparison_all <- rbindlist(lapply(comparison_files, fread), fill = TRUE)
final_models <- comparison_all[grepl("final", stage, ignore.case = TRUE)]
final_models <- final_models[order(-macro_f1)]

comparison_table <- final_models[, .(
  Model = model,
  Accuracy = f3(accuracy),
  `Balanced Accuracy` = f3(balanced_accuracy),
  `Macro-F1` = f3(macro_f1),
  `Draw Recall` = f3(recall_draw),
  `Draw F1` = f3(f1_draw)
)]

kable(comparison_table,
      caption = "Final model performance on the shared Final Test set")
```
